q-251064.name: Question 1
q-251064.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/fbccea4652fde939777bd69f621497f9e63ee79c7d4e4f0a5327bb141ce021ca.png)

In square units rounded to the nearest integer, the area of $△ABC$ is{{field-1}}.
q-251064.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of a right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

Notice that relative to the given angle $∠B,$ we have the length of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and need to determine the length of the adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $BC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({70}^{∘}) & =\frac{6}{BC} \\ BC\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({70}^{∘}) & =6 \\ BC & =\frac{6}{\operatorname{tan}⁡({70}^{∘})} \\ BC & =2.183…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot (2.183…) \\  & =6.551… \\  & ≈7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

q-28266.name: Question 3
q-28266.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/48cb6a248ab3ce706f26dc2e84e2feb337d509041c8b9756ea32fb3817aa097f.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=5,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-28266.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=5.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ 5 & =\frac{2x+4}{x-1} \\ 5(x-1) & =2x+4 \\ 5x-5 & =2x+4 \\ 3x & =9 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x+4=2(3)+4=10, \\ AC & =x-1=3-1=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 10 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

q-28266.html:
Question 3
?

Given that tan⁡(m∠A)=5, calculate the area (in square units) of △ABC shown above.

a
12
b
10
c
16
d
20
e
8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the area of the right triangle is A=12AC⋅BC.

We are given that tan⁡(m∠A)=5. Notice that relative to ∠A, we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side BC― and adjacent side AC―. Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for x: tan⁡(m∠A)=BCAC5=2x+4x−15(x−1)=2x+45x−5=2x+43x=9x=3

So, the side lengths are

BC=2x+4=2(3)+4=10,AC=x−1=3−1=2.

Therefore, the area of △ABC is A=12AC⋅BC=12⋅2⋅10=10.

q-76772.name: Question 4
q-76772.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/5ff3d7cda0ee3fbc807a4bacbd3a739d72d83d0020271936ba77e6afbc89b83f.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{5}{8},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-76772.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{5}{8}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{5}{8} & =\frac{3x-2}{4x} \\ 5(4x) & =8(3x-2) \\ 20x & =24x-16 \\ -4x & =-16 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =3x-2=3(4)-2=10, \\ AC & =4x=4(4)=16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16\cdot 10 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

q-54311.name: Question 5
q-54311.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/93489f5dd12c8dbbde799b4047965a89e4204f151c0b4dfc36286392775a05e2.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{4},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-54311.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{3}{4},$ where $\theta =m∠C.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{AC}$ adjacent to $∠C.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AB}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{AB}{AC} \\ \frac{3}{4} & =\frac{AB}{8} \\ AB & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot 8 \\ AB & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot AB \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 8\cdot 6 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-54310.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5},$ where $\theta =m∠B.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{AB}$ adjacent to $∠B.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{AC}{AB} \\ \frac{4}{5} & =\frac{AC}{10} \\ AC & =\frac{4}{5}\cdot 10 \\ AC & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\cdot 8 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC.

We are given that $m∠A={60}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({60}^{∘}) & =\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{3}\,x} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{3}\,x} \\ \sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,x) & =x+2 \\ 3x & =x+2 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =x+2=1+2=3, \\ AB & =\sqrt{3}\,x=\sqrt{3}(1)=\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
q-124469.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AB.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={30}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =\frac{2x}{\sqrt{3}\,x+3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} & =\frac{2x}{\sqrt{3}\,x+3} \\ \sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,x+3) & =3\cdot 2x \\ 3x+3\sqrt{3} & =6x \\ 3\sqrt{3} & =3x \\ x & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x=2\sqrt{3}, \\ AB & =\sqrt{3}\,x+3=\sqrt{3}\,(\sqrt{3})+3=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot BC\cdot AB \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{3}\cdot 6 \\  & =6\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-251195.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/243d382164750cdeb771f8630c3df642abcb034b3ddeb3c919f0b5f6b4fbff33.png)

In square units rounded to one decimal place, the area of $△ABC$ is{{field-1}}.
q-251195.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠B={72}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) & =\frac{3x+4}{2x-1} \\ (2x-1)\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) & =3x+4 \\ 2x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})-\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) & =3x+4 \\ x(2\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})-3) & =4+\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) \\ x & =\frac{4+\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})}{2\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})-3} \\ x & =2.243\,0…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x-1=2(2.243\,0…)-1=3.486\,1…, \\ AC & =3x+4=3(2.243\,0…)+4=10.729\,1….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(10.729\,1…)(3.486\,1…) \\  & =18.701\,3… \\  & ≈18.7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
